title: Attabad Lake
credits: Photos: Umar Farooq, Hasan Shaukat / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: High in the Karakoram, in Pakistan's Hunza valley, lies a lake that should not exist.
Before twenty ten, there was no lake here, only the Hunza River, running through a deep valley.
Then, in January twenty ten, a massive landslide came down from the mountains.
It buried homes in the village of Attabad, and blocked the river completely.
With nowhere to go, the water began to rise behind the landslide.
It flooded villages upstream, and drowned a long stretch of the Karakoram Highway.
Over the following months, the new lake grew, and its water turned a striking shade of turquoise.
Today, boats carry visitors across the water, beneath some of the highest mountains on Earth.
A lake born from a disaster has become one of Gilgit-Baltistan's best-known sights.
